findings.title: BuildIndex no longer serializes same-key builds
findings.body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the entire build. The lock now covers only the cache insert, and nothing single-flights a key. getOrCreateIndex is check-then-act (GetIndex, then BuildIndex if missing), and handleEvent plus Search can do that concurrently for a namespace that was not built at startup. Two BuildIndex calls for the same key both run bleve.New (file indexes collide on the same directory and the second New fails; memory indexes both succeed), both can pass the builder, and the later cache write overwrites the earlier *bleveIndex without closing it. Callers can also observe a nil index and start yet another build while the first is still running. TotalDocs ranges b.cache with no lock, so a concurrent cache write can panic the map. The old global lock was slow but prevented this; a per-key lock or singleflight is required, and every cache read must take cacheMu.

findings.title: Index init workers race on shared err
findings.body: init launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace, and each does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` on the single err variable from GetResourceStats, then returns that same err. totalBatchesIndexed++ is also unsynchronized. Concurrent assignment is a data race: a failed build can be overwritten by a later nil, so group.Wait can return success after a worker failed, or a spurious error can fail startup. This now runs inside NewResourceServer and a bad initErr aborts server creation, so the race decides whether the process starts. Each goroutine needs its own err variable; the counter needs atomic increment or to be computed after Wait.

findings.title: Failed constructor leaves background work running
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context, stores cancel on the server, then calls Init. On error it logs and returns nil without calling cancel or Stop. Init can already have started searchSupport's WatchWriteEvents poller (that one uses context.Background(), so cancel would not stop it anyway) and, if initWatcher ran, a broadcaster tied to s.ctx. The caller only receives an error and has no server handle to shut those goroutines down, so a failed startup leaks pollers and DB work for the process lifetime. Cancel and stop any watchers before returning the error, and tie the search watch to s.ctx instead of context.Background().

findings.title: Bleve BuildIndex span is not the parent of index work
findings.body: The PR's trace fix reassigns ctx from tracer.Start in searchSupport.init, searchSupport.build, and GetResourceStats, but BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. The span is ended, yet the context passed into the builder and ListIterator is the parent context, so the bleve BuildIndex span is a sibling of the DB and document-build spans rather than their parent. Any further bleve work in this function also will not carry the span. Use `ctx, span := b.tracer.Start(...)` and pass that ctx downward, matching the other call sites in this change.
